title: Sixel draws fails on certain height/width ratio
body:
### Issue description

When I try to use [chafa](https://github.com/hpjansson/chafa), sometimes the drawing fails (o it's cleaned too early) and I noticed that's correlated to the panel dimension

cat.jpg dimension: 1920x1080
failed panel dimension: 215x36

### Required information

* tmux version (`tmux -V`).
**tmux 3.6**
* Platform (`uname -sp`).
**Arch Linux 6.17.9-arch1-1**
* Terminal in use (xterm, rxvt, etc).
**foot**
* $TERM *inside* tmux (`echo $TERM`).
**screen-256color**
* $TERM *outside* tmux (`echo $TERM`).
**foot**
* Logs from tmux (`tmux kill-server; tmux -vv new`).
**ND**

comments.body:
> The original image has 1;1;1184;0 as the RA and it is the same in the cropped image, but that seems wrong, the new image should be smaller...

In Kw3C.txt/in.sixel.txt I see `1;1;1184;665`.  If it turns into `1;1;1184;0` as in bad2.sixel.txt, then somehow the height is disappearing - that's certainly a bug, but I cannot reproduce it.  What cell size does this happen with? (`printf '\033[16t';read`)

(The other issue might be related to overprinting.  With 10x20 cells on a 191x34 pane:

```
#!/bin/sh
cat in.sixel.txt
sleep 1
printf a
sleep 1
```

The cursor lands on the last line of the cat (as opposed to the next line).  `printf a` then erases the poor thing from existence (same thing happens with shell prompt).
On other pane heights, I get a cursor on the next line.  But I'm not sure if this is the right behavior, because xterm outside tmux always puts the cursor on the last line.)

comments.author: participant1
comments.body:
Yes, for me, if you are on the second line it is wrong, but on the first or third line it is OK:
~~~~
clear;echo;cat ~/in.sixel.txt # wrong
clear;cat ~/in.sixel.txt # OK
clear;echo;echo;cat ~/in.sixel.txt # OK
~~~~
But the funny thing is, the "wrong" behaviour is really sort of the *right* behaviour, because if you try the same outside tmux, you will see the prompt is left on the last line of the image, and overwrites it.

Removing the image straight away is not ideal, so it would really be better if we always just added an extra line...
